proposals.announcement_evidence: production of the Aviation Ground Power Unit 1.1
proposals.lexicon_quote: procurement dollars in the amount of $29.489M will procure Aviation Ground Power Unit (AGPU) 1.1 systems.  The Army Requirement Oversight Committee (ARO
proposals.rationale: This is a digest article with three paragraphs; the AGPU paragraph is Sun Test Systems Inc., Huntsville, Alabama, and its own contract number is W58RGZ-25-D-0019 (the chunk text is truncated just before it, but records.jsonl carries the full paragraph and ACC Redstone Arsenal as the contracting activity, which matches the aviation ground-support portfolio). The announcement names the article being produced by its exact designator, 'Aviation Ground Power Unit 1.1', and the procurement line 5212AZ3100 (Common Ground Equipment) says in its own narrative that its procurement dollars 'will procure Aviation Ground Power Unit (AGPU) 1.1 systems' - so the designator variant in the announcement is the line's own words, not an inferred resemblance. The award is for production, which is the procurement line's job rather than the Aviation Ground Support Equipment RDT&E line's; the one weakness a refute lens should weigh is that this is an IDIQ whose funding is determined with each order, so no appropriation colour is stated on the face of the announcement.

refute_a.reason: Money and mission both hold: the paragraph's scope is 'production of the Aviation Ground Power Unit 1.1' and the lake's base description for W58RGZ25D0019 reads 'AIRCRAFT PROCUREMENT APPROPRIATIONS FOR A SOLE SOURCE FIVE-YEAR IDIQ PRODUCTION CONTRACT OF THE AVIATION GROUND POWER UNIT, VERSION 1.1 (AGPU 1.1)' with PSC 'Aircraft Ground Servicing Equipment', which is exactly 5212AZ3100's own account (2031A, Aircraft Procurement, Army) and exactly what doc 343's justification says its procurement dollars buy ('will procure Aviation Ground Power Unit (AGPU) 1.1 systems'); AGPU is the article being produced, not a platform the contract merely supports, and Common Ground Equipment names AGPU 1.1 as its near-term priority rather than reading as a rollup or CATCHALL_TITLE line; the IDIQ's silence on colour does not cut the other way, because the only rival owner of the AGPU 1.1 designator (0605830A) sits in 2040A RDT&E and could not pay for an aircraft-procurement production award.

refute_b.reason: A different PE in the same index owns the announcement's exact designator: A.tsv row 'Aviation Ground Power Unit Next Generation (AGPU 1.1)' belongs to 0605830A (doc 355, Aviation Ground Support Equipment, ownership 'own', kind 'project'), while the proposed row is the plain 'Aviation Ground Power Unit (AGPU)' under 5212AZ3100 and reaches '1.1' only through its narrative sentence - the announcement's words 'Aviation Ground Power Unit 1.1' are literally the OTHER line's name, so the evidence links at least as well, arguably better, to 0605830A; nothing on the face of the award breaks the tie, because the paragraph (verified in records.jsonl: Sun Test Systems Inc., Huntsville, W58RGZ-25-D-0019, ACC Redstone Arsenal) states 'work locations and funding will be determined with each order' - no appropriation colour at all - and its cost-plus-fixed-fee component is as consistent with the RDT&E increment as with production.

proposals.announcement_evidence: development, qualification, and production of M1156E5 precision guidance kit
proposals.lexicon_quote: The Precision Guidance Kit (PGK) is a course correcting fuze that provides precision accurac
proposals.rationale: The announcement names 'precision guidance kit' outright and gives the Army's own designator for it, M1156E5 (PGK is the M1156 course-correcting fuze), and the action is a Northrop Grumman production/qualification mod obligating fiscal 2025 ammunition procurement, Army funds. 8750E27501 (Artillery Propellants, Fuzes and Primers) is the ammunition-procurement line whose narrative describes PGK as its own item - 'a course correcting fuze' - so the money colour on the award (procurement of ammunition) and the line agree. Three PEs in this index carry a PGK name, which a refute lens must test: 0604802A is RDT&E Eng Dev and cannot be paid with ammunition procurement funds, and 3102E89500's PGK sentence is a compatibility mention inside the 155mm projectile line ('as well as Precision Guidance Kit (PGK)') rather than a statement that the projectile line buys the kit. The fuze line is the one that buys the fuze.

refute_a.reason: The appropriation match is exact rather than merely compatible: the announcement obligates fiscal 2025 ammunition procurement, Army, the lake shows W15QKN13C0074 funded from 021-2034 and nothing else with PSC 'Fuzes and Primers' and base description 'TO AWARD PRODUCTION EFFORT FOR THE PRECISION GUIDANCE KIT (PGK)', and 8750E27501 is the 2034A Procurement of Ammunition, Army line whose own sub-item E99250 is 'ARTY, FUZE, PRECISION GUIDANCE KIT (PGK)' and whose narrative names the exact variant awarded ('The M1156E5, to become M1156A2 post Type Classification, will include anti-jam capability'); the kit is the item procured, not a platform the contract supports, and the line is a named fuze/propellant commodity line with per-item dollars rather than a catch-all — the development-and-qualification words in the scope raise no colour problem because the whole obligation is ammunition procurement, and the one same-account rival (3102E89500, the 155mm projectile line) is separated by mission, since the fuze line buys the fuze.

refute_b.reason: The name is owned three times over in this one index and the announcement's evidence does not pick between the owners: 0604802A (doc 355, Weapons and Munitions - Eng Dev) owns the byte-identical string 'The Precision Guidance Kit (PGK)' plus 'Long Range-Precision Guidance Kit (LR-PGK) Development', and 3102E89500 (doc 349) owns 'Precision Guidance Kit (PGK)', alongside the proposed 8750E27501 row; the announcement offers only the bare phrase 'precision guidance kit' and the increment designator M1156E5, which NO index row names, and its own verbs - 'development, qualification, and production' against a 2013 ACC-Newark development contract being modified (P00099) - match the Eng Dev owner's project language at least as well as the fuze-procurement line, so the only thing separating the three owners is appropriation colour, which is lens A's ground and not identity evidence.

proposals.announcement_evidence: sustainment and support for the fielded modernization of enterprise terminals and AN/GSC-52 medium satellite communications terminal modernization programs
proposals.lexicon_quote: The Modernization of Enterprise Terminals (MET), BB8501/Enterprise Wideband Satellite Terminal Digital EQ,
proposals.rationale: The announcement spells the program name out in the line's own words - 'modernization of enterprise terminals' is MET, and AN/GSC-52 is the legacy enterprise terminal MET replaces - so this is a named program, not an unnamed services ceiling. 2948BB8500 (Defense Enterprise Wideband Satcom Systems) owns MET in its narrative. The award obligates fiscal 2020 other procurement, Army alongside O&M, so procurement colour is present on the action and intersects the line. The honest weakness for a refute lens is the word 'sustainment': part of the money is O&M, and O&M sustainment attached to a procurement line is the documented failure mode - if the refuting lens reads the whole scope as post-fielding sustainment rather than the modernization programme itself, this should fall.

refute_a.reason: Refuted as the documented failure mode — O&M sustainment attached to a procurement line: the award's own words buy 'sustainment and support for the fielded' MET and AN/GSC-52 programs on a cost-no-fee/cost-plus-fixed-fee vehicle, the announcement names operations and maintenance, Army first and gives no separate OPA figure, and the lake confirms the species with base description 'MET SUSTAINMENT SUPPORT UCA', a services PSC ('IT and Telecom - Annual Software Maintenance Service Plans'), and 14 funding accounts spanning Navy 017, Army O&M 021-2020, Air Force 057 and Defense-wide 097 against $262M of lifetime obligations — a joint post-fielding support vehicle, not the $45M of BB8416 acquisition work that 2948BB8500 (2035A, Other Procurement, Army) budgets; that 021-2035 appears somewhere in that account list clears the loader's mechanical guard but does not make this action the line's own work, and 2948BB8500 is in any case the DEWSS parent that doc 346 says 'consists of' four separately budgeted efforts (B08900, BB8416, BB8501, BB8509), so post-fielding sustainment charged partly to the aggregate does not support the claim that this action paid for this program element's own work.

refute_b.reason: No alternative owner survives inspection: 2948BB8500 is the ONLY row in A.tsv whose name contains 'Enterprise Terminals' ('The Modernization of Enterprise Terminals (MET)', doc 346, ownership 'own'), the bare acronym MET does collide with 'The Medium Equipment Trailer (MET)' (8309DA0500) and 'M1311 Medium Equipment Trailer (MET)' (8992DA0924) but that collision is unreachable because the announcement spells the program out in full, and AN/GSC-52 is the legacy enterprise terminal MET replaces rather than a rival program name (no index row owns 'GSC-52'); the alias is real, not invented, and this is not a variant/increment mismatch or a contractor-name match. Two caveats I could not convert into a refutation and that lens A should weigh: the lexicon quote trails into a sibling BLI ('MET, BB8501/Enterprise Wideband Satellite Terminal Digital EQ') and the row is flagged name_repaired, so the P-doc sentence may enumerate the BB85xx family rather than assert BB8500 alone - but BB8501 is not an index row, so there is no better owner to prefer; and the F index carries 'AIR FORCE WIDEBAND ENTERPRISE TERMINALS (AFWET)' (MILSAT, doc 416) whose narrative also names MET, which is a cross-org mention, not an owner this Army-let action (ACC Rock Island, OMA + other procurement, Army) could be reassigned to. The scope word 'sustainment' on a fielded program is the real hazard here and it is lens A's question, not mine.

The announcement obligates fiscal 2016 operations and maintenance, Army funds, while 6500GA0750 is a procurement (WTCV) line; a buy of 45 sets of legacy components on O&M reads as replenishment for fielded tanks, not as the upgrade line executing SEP conversions. The index row is also a bare title - its lexicon quote is the title itself, with no narrative body naming a sensor generation - so there is nothing in the PE's own words to confirm that its IFLIR and the announcement's Third Generation FLIR are the same increment. A second FLIR owner exists in this same index (Block 1 Second Generation FLIR under the Abrams Upgrade Program), which is direct evidence that generation labels here distinguish programs rather than decorate one. Scope is also mostly technical, engineering, test and logistics services. Not enough to assert attribution.
